title: RAKR: A Reflection-Based Agent for Adaptive Knowledge Rewriting Technology Applied to Knowledge Graph Question Answering
venue: 2025 11th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA) systems leverage structured knowledge to answer natural language questions. However, they still face challenges in bridging the gap between knowledge representation and the understanding of language models when dealing with complex queries. This paper introduces a Reflexion Augmented Knowledge Rewriting (RAKR) framework, which integrates chain-of-thought reasoning, a reflection mechanism, and structured knowledge operations. RAKR achieves dynamic semantic transformation of subgraphs in knowledge graphs by introducing an intelligent agent capable of performing precise reasoning planning, relationship exploration, and knowledge organization. The innovation of RAKR lies in its dual-layer reflection loop mechanism: the open-ended reflection before generation for immediate iterative optimization, and the closed-loop reflection after generation for constructing long-term memory used for subsequent question retrieval. Compared to existing methods, RAKR not only generates structured knowledge representations that adhere to reasoning pathways but also possesses the capability to continuously optimize knowledge rewriting strategies through feedback from historical interactions. Additionally, we propose a Differentiated Preference Alignment (DAPA) training method, which combines supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning based on human feedback, significantly improving the quality of knowledge rewriting. Experimental results demonstrate that RAKR substantially outperforms existing methods on KGQA benchmark tests, particularly achieving up to a 10.2% increase in accuracy when handling complex questions requiring multi-hop reasoning. This research provides a new paradigm for knowledge rewriting techniques and offers an effective pathway for the deep integration of large language models and structured knowledge.
